name: physics-gravity-rest-height
asserts: THE LANE'S ONLY DYNAMICS GATE -- do not skip it without replacing it. Expected verdict: exactly one 'OK: gravity_rest_height' line in tests/output.txt (run_smoke.py greps for it; the harness has no per-world expected-verdict field, hence this note). It grades three MEASURED NUMBERS against closed-form expectations derived from the world's own authored fields, so it can never be re-goldened to whatever the engine currently does: (1) free-fall acceleration recovered from the second difference of the faller's own z trajectory, z[k+1]-2z[k]+z[k-1] = -g dt^2, which is exact for a constant-acceleration integrator and therefore carries no integrator-convention bias -- expected = WorldInfo.gravity read live, tolerance 1%; this is what the 'gravity was never plumbed into Newton, every world ran at -9.81 regardless of WorldInfo.gravity' defect trips, and what a no-physics inert stub trips (g_est = 0). (2) Rest height = floor_top + half the faller's box, tolerance 6 mm (default soft contact penetrates about m*g/ke = 3.9 mm). The floor's top face is at z=0.5 ON PURPOSE: a floor at z=0 was masked by Newton's then-UNCONDITIONAL implicit ground plane, which is how the statics-off defect hid -- with statics broken the box lands near z=0.1 (builds before 2026-08-12) or never stops at all (builds after: the implicit plane is now added only to substitute for a dropped authored Plane collider, and this world's floor is a Box, so there is nothing to substitute for), missing by >= 100 mm either way. newtonStatics is deliberately left UNSET so the shipped DEFAULT is what gets graded. (3) A motorised HingeJoint reaches its commanded 0.6 rad, cross-checked against the arm link's absolute world position, so a sensor echoing its own setpoint cannot pass. Controller is PYTHON on purpose: the four C-controller physics worlds that would otherwise have filled this hole (damping, hinge_joint_damping, rolling_friction, floating_point_precision) are unrunnable in a clone whose test controllers are not built, and that failure surfaces only as a 30 s 'results file has not been written' timeout. MEASURED 2026-08-08 on LAPTOP-H61DJILS (RTX 3060 laptop), binary 51b8aaa5, solver 'MuJoCo (cpu/mj_step, default)', bit-identical across repeat runs: g=9.8124 vs 9.8100 expected (2.4% of a 1% budget), rest z=0.599892 vs 0.600000 (0.108 mm penetration, 1.8% of the 6 mm budget), hinge 0.6012 rad sensor / 0.6020 rad geometric vs 0.6000 commanded. These are a reference for a future reader, NOT a golden the tolerances were fitted to -- every bound is derived from a physical model, so do not retune one to accommodate a drift. NEGATIVE CONTROLS RUN, so the gate is known to be able to fail: OMNISIM_NEWTON_STATICS=0 fires assertion 2 -- RE-MEASURED 2026-08-13 (tree 227b35c36, binary sha256[:16] 1b82affcd3956d95, machine 9722d23d12a3): the box no longer lands anywhere, reading z=-3.039 at step 240 and z=-287.959 at step 1920 and still accelerating. This note used to say it 'lands at z=0.099892 on the implicit plane (83x the tolerance)', which was true until 2026-08-12, when the implicit z=0 ground plane stopped being unconditional and became a substitution for a dropped authored Plane collider; this world's floor is a Box, so there is nothing to substitute for. THE GATE IS UNAFFECTED -- only the number changed, and a box at -287 m misses the 6 mm rest-height budget by rather more than 0.0999 did. OMNISIM_NEWTON_GROUND_PLANE=1 reproduces the old landing exactly if you need the historical control; deleting the faller's Physics node gives g_est=-0.000000 and fires assertion 1; a RotationalMotor with no minPosition/maxPosition sits at 0.003532 rad and fires assertion 3 (that one was not hypothetical -- this backend configures a limitless motor as a VELOCITY wheel and ignores setPosition, which is how the world was first authored). Cost: about 5 s wall clock, 2.4 s of sim time at basicTimeStep 4. NOTE FOR THE NEXT PERSON: this is the FIRST tests/physics world in the lane, so run_smoke.py now drives TWO test groups, and test_suite.py asserts per group that the engine logged a port-fallback line containing BOTH '1234' and '1235' -- an assertion only the first group can satisfy if anything else is squatting on 1235. It passed 3 consecutive clean runs, but a leftover killed omnisim-bin holding 1235 turns a green physics result into 'FAILURE: OmniSim listened on a port that was in use'. Check the port table before blaming the physics.

name: physics-wheel-roll-noslip
asserts: THE LANE'S ONLY WHEEL GATE -- it asserts that a driven wheel's ROTATION accounts for the chassis's MOTION. Expected verdict: exactly one 'OK: wheel_roll_noslip' line in tests/output.txt. WHY IT EXISTS: until it, nothing anywhere in this repo asserted that a wheel TURNED. Every other check asks only whether the body MOVED -- a headless PASS, a displacement assertion, a 'drove to the goal' verdict, a benchmark grader -- and a robot dragging itself along on four frozen wheels satisfies all of them. One in this tree did exactly that for its whole life: a 4-wheel rover crossing an arena at 1.0-1.6 m/s while its four wheel hinges turned at ~0.14 rad/s, which at the authored 0.08 m radius is 0.011 m/s of rolling, i.e. 99.3% slip, and nothing noticed. FOUR ASSERTIONS (tests/physics/controllers/wheel_roll_noslip/): (1) the rover actually drives, |v| >= 0.15 m/s -- a world where nothing moves satisfies no-slip trivially (0 == 0) so grading one is refused; (2) no-slip on VELOCITIES, |omega*r - v| <= 0.35*|v|; (3) no-slip on the INTEGRALS, wheel angle travelled x r vs the chassis's net displacement, which involves no differentiation anywhere and so cannot be a sampling artefact; (4) the PositionSensor's differentiated omega agrees with the wheel Solid's own angular velocity read through the supervisor and de-rotated by the chassis -- a sensor echoing its own setpoint passes 2 and 3 and fails 4. The wheel RADIUS is read from the scene's own boundingObject, never hardcoded. THE 0.35 TOLERANCE IS NOT FITTED: it sits in the empty gap between two measured populations -- healthy hand-authored wheeled worlds across this tree score 0.00-0.18, the sliding defect scores 0.60-1.00 (docs/developer/roll-check.md). DO NOT REPLACE ANY OF THIS WITH A STICTION/TORQUE FORMULA: the failing rover had 0.4 N.m on each of four wheels against 3.6 kg, ~5.6 m/s^2 of nominally available traction, which should have been ample. MEASURED 2026-08-10 on LAPTOP-H61DJILS (RTX 3060 laptop), binary omnisim-bin-fixed.exe, solver 'mujoco': v_body 0.450 m/s, omega 5.000 rad/s x r=0.09 = 0.450 m/s of rolling, slip 0.0%. These are a reference, NOT a golden the tolerance was fitted to. NEGATIVE CONTROL RUN, so the gate is known to be able to fail: scripts/dev/roll_check_assets/wheel_roll_slip_negative_control.omniworld is this world with maxTorque 12 -> 0.4 AND basicTimeStep 8 -> 16 AND newtonSubsteps 4 removed, and it measures 60-65% slip; `python scripts/dev/roll_check.py --self-test` runs the pair and requires opposite verdicts. IT TAKES ALL THREE EDITS -- maxTorque 0.4 alone rolls (0.000), a 16 ms single-substep integration alone rolls (0.001), only the interaction slides. That is why the check is behavioural: no torque formula predicts a dependence on the timestep. Cost: about 3 s wall clock, 2.7 s of sim time at basicTimeStep 8. The rover is COPIED from DEF ROLL in projects/robot_combat/worlds/tests/drive_test.omniworld (the repo's known-good roller) so that a red here means the engine changed, not that the gate was mis-authored. ⚠️ IF THIS GOES RED WITH 'the rover barely moved', SUSPECT THE BINARY BEFORE THE PHYSICS. Measured 2026-08-10: on omnisim-bin.clampfast.exe (an engine build from the day before) the same world reads body 0.007 m/s / wheels 0.080 rad/s -- the rover never moves at all, because on that build a motor target set AFTER the Newton world is finalised has no effect (the regression documented in tests/benchmarks/agentbench/.../r1_drive_probe/r1_drive_probe.py and fixed since). That is a TRUE negative -- an engine that cannot turn a wheel should fail a wheel gate -- but the fix is to rebuild, not to touch this world. ⚠️ ALSO NOT YET VERIFIED: everything here was measured on msys64/mingw64/bin/omnisim-bin-fixed.exe, because a parallel lane was running the stock omnisim-bin.exe and it was off-limits. tests/test_suite.py hardcodes omnisim-bin.exe, so this gate has NOT been run end-to-end on the binary the pre-push hook actually launches; it was verified by running the world directly against the fixed engine and confirming exactly one 'OK: wheel_roll_noslip' line reached tests/output.txt. First person with that binary free: run `python tests/smoke/run_smoke.py --nomake`.

name: api-accelerometer
skip_reason: RED, and the cause is NOT what this note used to say. The previous reason blamed Newton for hardcoding up_axis=Axis.Z and never reading WorldInfo.coordinateSystem -- that defect was REAL but was FIXED in commit c77cbe98, and this world proves the fix works: its engine log reads '[OmNewtonBackend] WorldInfo.coordinateSystem "NUE" -> up_axis Y: gravity direction and the implicit ground-plane normal follow it' (re-measured 2026-08-08 on LAPTOP-H61DJILS / RTX 3060 laptop). So gravity IS on the world's own up axis and the old explanation would send the next person down a dead end. WHAT IS ACTUALLY WRONG IS NOT YET ROOT-CAUSED. The controller exits 1, and the engine emits four warnings of the form 'Parent of Accelerometer node has no physics: measurements may be wrong' for the center/tX/tY/tZ-offset sensors -- they sit under a HingeJoint endPoint chain whose intermediate Solids carry no Physics node, so under Newton's registration fold their parent owns no body. That is the lead worth pulling, not the coordinate system. Also verified PRE-EXISTING and not caused by the ODE deletion: it fails identically with physicsBackend "ode" restored, and (separately) OMNISIM_FORCE_ODE is now ignored outright -- the run writes a normal .newton.json sidecar with backend=newton. Un-skip when the accelerometer's parent-physics problem is fixed; do NOT retune the expected values, the assertion (+9.8 on Y for a stationary NUE sensor) is correct.

name: physics-contact-points
skip_reason: RED ON NEWTON, and there is no longer any pin that changes that. Built on ODE-path WorldInfo.contactProperties (softCFM / softERP / bounce), which the Newton backend ignores; on Newton the cone settles differently and the verdict '-rotation[3] > 2.44' (contact_points.c:22) fails. Measured 2026-08-08 on machine LAPTOP-H61DJILS (RTX 3060 laptop) with the in-binary OMNISIM_PROBE_TRAJ probe over 3000 ms: on the default backend (sidecar {backend:newton, solver:'MuJoCo (cpu/mj_step, default)', finalised:true}) the Cone travels from its authored -5.951940 -4.392650 1.060230 to -5.976457 -5.292823 0.007408, i.e. it rolls down the ramp and lands -- physically plausible, just not what the ODE-era threshold was cut for. HISTORY WORTH KEEPING, because it is why this world is skipped rather than re-pinned: on an earlier build the same day, OMNISIM_FORCE_ODE=1 made this test PASS by producing no physics at all -- no .newton.json sidecar and the Cone bit-identical to t=0 after 3000 ms -- because the authored rotation (-2.4871, world line 117) already satisfies '> 2.44' before anything happens. A green verdict from a frozen scene is worse than a red one. The engine now ignores that var (same-day rebuild), so the trap is closed, but do not go looking for a pin to reopen it. Un-skip when the cone/ramp verdict is re-goldened against Newton contacts, which requires establishing the analytically correct settle angle -- not retuning the threshold to whatever Newton currently does.

name: rendering-normals
skip_reason: Offscreen Camera framebuffers under --no-rendering contain only the viewport clear color (=Background.skyColor), not the rendered scene geometry. With atmosphericSky in the world the clear is (4,4,4) so all 7 cameras are byte-identical and every diff is 0; the diff(c0,c6) > 10000 assertion fails. Replacing atmosphericSky with a plain skyColor only flips the test outcome based on whether edge-antialiasing of the cleared rect happens to exceed 10000 (passes at [0.9,0.1,0.1] -> diff 15714; fails at [0.5,0.5,0.5] -> diff 3421) -- no actual geometry shading is captured either way. The atmospheric-sky migration just exposed this -- the pre-migration cubemap skybox masked the same renderer bug by drawing a photo background. The earlier OmSolidDevice postFinalize NULL-deref crash masked it further by aborting before the assertion. Real fix is in the WREN offscreen camera render path: wr_scene_render_to_viewports() during a controller step needs to actually include scene geometry when the main 3D view's render loop is suppressed. Restore after that is fixed.
